disease_name: Bacterial Blight / Angular Leaf Spot / Blackarm
symptoms: Angular water-soaked spots delimited by leaf veinlets; spots turn brown to dark purplish-black. On stems, elongated black lesions ('blackarm phase') weaken branch junctions and cause breakage. Internal boll rot and discolored stained lint.
favorable_conditions: Warm and wet weather, day temperatures 30-35°C, high humidity (>85%), wind-driven rains during flowering.
risk_factors: Infected fuzzy seeds, high nitrogen fertilization, overhead rainstorms beating foliage.
prevention: Acid delinting of cotton seeds with concentrated sulphuric acid (100ml/kg fuzzy seed) followed by seed dressing with Streptocycline (100 ppm).
management: Foliar spray with Copper Oxychloride 50 WP @ 2.5g/L combined with Streptocycline @ 0.1g/L (1g in 10L water). Repeat after 15 days if rainy weather continues.

symptoms: Pale translucent angular spots on upper leaf surface bounded by veinlets; dense white frosty powdery fungal growth appears on underside of leaves resembling chalk powder (Dahiya). Leaves turn yellow and drop prematurely.
favorable_conditions: Humid cool weather during boll development (RH >80%, temp 20-25°C), dense foliage.
risk_factors: Over-fertilization with N, high plant density, prolonged late monsoon wet spells.
prevention: Proper row spacing (90x60 cm), clean cultivation, balanced potash application.
management: Foliar spray with Wettable Sulphur 80% WP @ 2.5g/L or Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1.0g/L or Kresoxim-methyl 44.3% SC @ 1.0ml/L upon first symptom appearance.
